memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who live there will be
appalled. I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out my sword
and pursue you. Your land will be laid waste, and your cities will lie in
ruins'" - Lev 26:32-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The heaviest of the consequences arrives: exile. The people would be
scattered among the nations, the land left desolate, the cities in ruins.
For Israel, whose whole identity was tied to this land, exile was the
deepest possible loss.

History records that this came to pass. The people were carried off to
Babylon, and the land lay in ruins. God's warnings were not idle threats;
they were the honest truth spoken in advance.

Yet even here, in the depths of judgment, we must not miss what God did
not say. He did not say, I will destroy you completely. He did not say,
this is the end of My people. Scattering is not the same as abandoning.

Dear reader, this is vital for understanding the God of the Bible. Even in
His severest discipline, He does not cast off His people forever. The exile
was real, but so was the promise of return. Through Jeremiah, spoken during
that very exile, God said, I know the plans I have for you, plans to
prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future (Jer
29:11).

For the believer in Christ, the assurance goes even deeper. Jesus said,
whoever comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37), and no one can
snatch His sheep out of His hand (John 10:28).

You may go through a scattering season — loss, upheaval, a life in ruins.
But if you belong to Christ, you are never abandoned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I sometimes fear that God has abandoned me in a hard season?
2. What "scattering" or loss am I walking through right now?
3. How does knowing Christ never drives me away steady me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, even in Your discipline You never abandon Your people. In my
seasons of loss and upheaval, help me trust that in Christ I am held and
never cast away. Amen.
